title: Inheritance: Security Droid Upgrade
objectives: Create specialized classes from base classes
Add new methods to child classes
description: Upgrade your Worker Bots into specialized Security Units! Learn inheritance - how child classes can inherit all the features of a parent class, then add their own unique abilities. Create a SecurityDroid that has everything a Droid has, PLUS patrol capabilities.

exercises.title: Create a Child Class
exercises.instructions:
**Security Division Upgrade Protocol:**

Create a SecurityDroid that inherits from Droid.

**Instructions:**
1. First, copy the base Droid class (with __init__ and greet)
2. Create a new class `SecurityDroid` that inherits from Droid:
   ```python
   class SecurityDroid(Droid):
       pass
   ```
3. Create a SecurityDroid: `guard = SecurityDroid('GUARD-X1', 100)`
4. Call `guard.greet()`

**Magic:** SecurityDroid automatically gets ALL of Droid's methods!
exercises.expectedOutput: Greetings. I am GUARD-X1, Worker Unit.
hints: The word in parentheses is the parent class
'pass' means the class has no extra code yet

exercises.title: Add Specialized Methods to Child
exercises.instructions:
**Security Features Installation:**

Give SecurityDroid its own unique patrol() method.

**Task:**
1. Use your Droid and SecurityDroid classes
2. Add a `patrol()` method to SecurityDroid that prints:
   `"[{self.name}] Initiating sector patrol. All clear."`
3. Create a SecurityDroid: `security = SecurityDroid('SENTINEL-9', 98)`
4. Call BOTH methods: `security.greet()` AND `security.patrol()`

**Result:** SecurityDroid has inherited greet() PLUS its own patrol()!
exercises.expectedOutput:
Greetings. I am SENTINEL-9, Worker Unit.
[SENTINEL-9] Initiating sector patrol. All clear.
hints: Add the patrol method inside SecurityDroid class
Use self.name just like in the parent class
Child classes can have methods the parent doesn't have

exercises.title: Compare Worker vs Security Units
exercises.instructions:
**Factory Comparison Test:**

Create both types of droids and see the difference!

**Test Procedure:**
1. Create a regular Droid: `worker = Droid('WORKER-5', 100)`
2. Create a SecurityDroid: `guard = SecurityDroid('GUARD-5', 100)`
3. Make the worker greet
4. Make the guard greet AND patrol
5. Try to make worker.patrol() - it will error! (Comment it out after testing)

**Observation:** Workers can't patrol (they don't have that method), but Guards can do BOTH jobs!
exercises.solution:
class Droid:
    def __init__(self, name, battery_level):
        self.name = name
        self.battery_level = battery_level
    
    def greet(self):
        print(f"Greetings. I am {self.name}, Worker Unit.")

class SecurityDroid(Droid):
    def patrol(self):
        print(f"[{self.name}] Initiating sector patrol. All clear.")

# Create both types
worker = Droid('WORKER-5', 100)
guard = SecurityDroid('GUARD-5', 100)

# Test their capabilities
print("=== Worker Capabilities ===")
worker.greet()
# worker.patrol()  # Would error - workers can't patrol!

print("\n=== Guard Capabilities ===")
guard.greet()  # Inherited
guard.patrol()  # Unique to SecurityDroid
exercises.expectedOutput:
=== Worker Capabilities ===
Greetings. I am WORKER-5, Worker Unit.

=== Guard Capabilities ===
Greetings. I am GUARD-5, Worker Unit.
[GUARD-5] Initiating sector patrol. All clear.
hints: Workers only have methods from the Droid class
SecurityDroids have Droid methods PLUS patrol()
This is inheritance: child gets parent's features + its own
